title: [Self Promotion] I developed a complex Poker Automation Strategy game using an AI-integrated workflow (Cursor + Claude). Here is the result.
author: Capable-Rice
selftext:
Hi r/aigamedev!

I am a solo developer of SUITE: The Automated Card Engine, which just released a free demo on Steam.

I wanted to share my experience of building a strategy game with a complex logic system using AI-Assisted Development.



The Workflow:

Coding(React + TypeScript):

I initially started prototyping with Cursor, but midway through, I switched to Claude Code(Anthropic's coding agent) for deeper implementation.

While Cursor was great for quick edits, Claude Code acted more like a Senior Partner. I focused on the Architecture—defining the GameState, Zustand stores, and poker logic—and let Claude Code handle the heavy lifting of implementing complex UI components and refactoring.

Art & Assets: The pixel art style was initially generated using AI image tools, then manually refined and animated to ensure a consistent game feel.

Audio: SFX and BGM were drafted using AI tools to match the Casino/Factory atmosphere.



About the Game:

It's a mix of Balatro and Factorio. You don't play cards manually; you design the deck order and equip workstations to automate the scoring process.



Steam Demo (Free):

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4334020/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4334020/)



This project demonstrates how AI tools can empower solo devs to build complex systems that would usually require a larger team.

I'd love to discuss the workflow or get feedback on the game!

comments.author: yjgoh28
comments.body:
this looks amazing! mind sharing more details how you created the art and assets? 

eg: which tool u use? did you created animation and how? how do you get good consistency. 

this demo shows very good uiux design.

replies.author: Capable-Rice
replies.body:
Thanks for the kind words!

The art is generated with nanobanana pro and then retouched in Photoshop. SFX are made using the Web Audio API oscillator, and while it’s not in this video, the BGM was created with Suno AI.

Most animations are AI-generated, with detailed prompts and multiple iterations.  
For consistency, I rely heavily on documentation—game structure, key ideas, and milestones are documented and continuously referenced by Claude.

UI consistency was achieved by implementing everything in CSS rather than AI-generated images, centralizing UI components and shared styles.  
Asset consistency comes from modularization (using base templates and central reference images).

Since I was aware of AI’s limitations with visual consistency, I chose a Balatro-like genre, where strong character-specific assets aren’t critical. I believe understanding AI’s limitations and designing around them is a key part of using AI effectively in projects.
